'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Four bombings in the [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] capital [[Kabul]] kill at least four people, including a district police chief and his bodyguard. Three others are reportedly wounded. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attacks/four-blasts-hit-kabul-district-police-chief-among-the-dead-idUSKBN2AA1MQ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Red Cross]] officials report that 80% of Tigray's 6 million people are unreachable. In the regional capital of [[Mekelle]], which is now home to 250,000 [[internally displaced person|displaced people]], [[vaccine]]s have expired and there are no longer any [[HIV]] or [[tuberculosis]] drugs. [https://apnews.com/article/ethiopia-tigray-starvation-bc4b3d569137925c5c34d30ac1683664 (Associated Press)] [https://www.eepa.be/?p=4730 (''Europe External Programme with Africa'')]
**[[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] (TPLF) forces [[ambush]] [[Ethiopia]]n and [[Eritrea]]n troops in May Keyah, 50–60 kilometers south of [[Mekelle]]. Fighting between the TPLF and Ethiopia is also reported in Guya, [[Kola Tembien]]. [https://www.eepa.be//wp-content/uploads/2020/11/Situation-Report-EEPA-Horn-No.-81-10-February-2021.pdf (''Europe External Programme with Africa'')]
*[[Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict (2015–present)|Saudi Arabian–Yemeni border conflict]]
**The [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] carry out a [[drone strike]] on [[Abha International Airport]] in [[Saudi Arabia]], damaging a civilian aircraft. A Houthi spokesman says that the attack is in response to [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen|coalition]] [[airstrike]]s and other actions in [[Yemen]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-yemen-security-saudi-airport/yemens-houthis-say-they-carried-out-drone-attack-on-saudi-airport-idUSKBN2AA1IG?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sriwijaya Air Flight 182]]
**[[Indonesia]]'s [[National Transportation Safety Committee]] issues a preliminary report into the crash of Sriwijaya Air Flight 182, which reveals that a malfunctioning cockpit throttle caused the left engine of the aircraft to lose power before it plunged into the [[Java Sea]]. [https://www.voanews.com/east-asia-pacific/preliminary-report-issued-deadly-crash-indonesian-jetliner (Voice of America)]
*[[List of earthquakes in 2021|Earthquakes in 2021]]
**A magnitude 7.7 [[earthquake]] strikes off the [[Loyalty Islands Province]], [[New Caledonia]]. It is the strongest recorded earthquake of the year so far. A [[tsunami warning]] was issued with the [[Australian Bureau of Meteorology]] confirming that a [[tsunami]] was generated by the earthquake. [https://www.sfchronicle.com/local/earthquakes/quake-alerts/article/Magnitude-7-5-earthquake-strikes-southeast-of-the-15939087.php (''The San Francisco Chronicle'')] [https://metro.co.uk/2021/02/10/new-zealand-tsunami-warning-after-7-9-earthquake-strikes-nearby-14057100/ (''Metro'')] [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/tsunami-confirmed-after-7-7-magnitude-earthquake-in-south-pacific-report-2367789 (NDTV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]] 
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the San Francisco Bay Area]], [[501.V2 variant]]
******[[California]] reports its first two cases of the 501.V2 variant in people from [[Alameda County, California|Alameda County]] and [[Santa Clara County, California|Santa Clara County]]. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-02-10/first-cases-of-south-african-coronavirus-strain-found-in-california (''The Los Angeles Times'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
*****[[Florida]] surpasses 300 cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://patch.com/florida/bradenton/u-k-covid-19-variant-surges-florida-more-300-cases (Patch.com)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maine]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
*****[[Maine]] reports its first two cases of the B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the [[United Kingdom]] in a person from [[Franklin County, Maine|Franklin County]] who previously travelled internationally. [https://www.pressherald.com/2021/02/10/first-case-of-covid-19-variant-has-reached-maine/ (''Portland Press Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] approves the use of [[China]]'s [[Sinovac]] and [[CanSino Biologics|CanSino]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-mexico-cansino/mexico-approves-chinas-cansino-and-sinovac-covid-19-vaccines-idUSKBN2AA12W (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bahrain]]
****[[Bahrain]] approves the emergency use of [[Russia]]'s [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[vaccine]], becoming the fourth vaccine to be approved in the country. [https://www.bna.bh/en/news?cms=q8FmFJgiscL2fwIzON1%2BDnj3nlhO%2FnNA3AJepa%2B590k%3D (Bahrain News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] launches a vaccination campaign against [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] using 600,000 doses of [[Sinopharm]]'s [[BBIBP-CorV]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. The son of [[Prime Minister of Cambodia|Prime Minister]] [[Hun Sen]], Hun Manet, and several cabinet ministers are among the first people to get vaccinated. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Spotlight/Coronavirus/Cambodia-COVID-vaccinations-begin-with-Hun-Sen-s-sons-ministers (Nikkei Asia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] will reopen [[theme park]]s and sports and entertainment facilities, as well as extend dining hours in restaurants to 10:00 p.m. local time beginning February 18 as the number of cases continues to decline. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/hong-kong-ease-covid-19-restrictions-daily-cases-decline-14162640 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****A pet dog owned by a [[COVID-19]] patient in [[South Korea]] tests positive for COVID-19 after it showed symptoms. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-southkorea-pets/south-korean-dog-has-its-coronavirus-test-day-idUSKBN2AA1CB (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****[[Croatia]] detects the first case of UK variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in a samples from three people including a three-year-old children. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-02-croatia-cases-british-virus-variant.amp (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The [[Government of Germany|federal government]] and leaders of 16 [[States of Germany|German states]] agree to extend the nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until March 7 due to concerns about [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]] despite a decline in the number of new cases. [https://www.dw.com/en/covid-germany-extends-lockdown-until-march/a-56520479 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Portugal]] reports its first two identified cases of COVID-19 infection with the Lineage P.1 [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]], both of which were detected in the [[Lisbon metropolitan area]]. [https://www.rtp.pt/noticias/pais/variante-brasileira-novos-casos-em-portugal_v1296549 (RTP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] surpasses four million cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], becoming the fourth country to do so after the [[United States]], [[India]], and [[Brazil]]. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/02/10/russias-virus-caseload-passes-4-million-a72893 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination programme in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Charles, Prince of Wales]] and [[Camilla, Duchess of Cornwall]] receive their first doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-56008436 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***The [[New Zealand Government]] grants a formal approval of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] and announces that high-risk groups such as [[quarantine]] personnel, frontline health workers and airline staff will be the first to receive the vaccine. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-10/covid-19-vaccine-pfizer-gets-full-approval-in-new-zealand/13140196 (ABC Australia)]
**The [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) recommends the use of [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] by all adults worldwide, including people over age of 65 and recommends an interval of 8 to 12 weeks between the doses. [https://www.ft.com/content/be33aa38-5eff-4069-b104-ba7bdb735c72 (''Financial Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Myanmar–United States relations]], [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces sanctions on the [[Tatmadaw|military]] leaders who directed the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] in [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/myanmar-coup-biden-sanctions/ (CBS News)]
*[[Nuclear program of Iran]]
**The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] confirms that [[Iran]] has carried out its plan to produce [[uranium metal]] at a nuclear facility in [[Isfahan]], a major breach of the 2015 [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|Iran nuclear deal]]. Uranium metal is essential to making the core of a [[nuclear weapon]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-nuclear-iaea/iran-produces-uranium-metal-iaea-says-in-latest-breach-of-deal-idUSKBN2AA2P6?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Pakistan]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Pakistan]] commutes the [[death sentence]]s of two [[schizophrenic]] prisoners after considering that if their illness makes them unable to comprehend the rationale of their crimes, the death sentence will not meet the ends of justice. The ruling is celebrated by [[human rights]] groups. [https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-top-court-bars-execution-of-two-mentally-ill-prisoners/a-56520241 (DW)]
*[[2021 Russian protests]]
**A court in [[Russia]] orders the arrest of [[Alexei Navalny]]'s ally [[Leonid Volkov (politician)|Leonid Volkov]] for "appealing to minors to join illegal protests". Volkov, who lives in the [[European Union]] and who will not be [[extradite]]d, said on [[Facebook]] that he will "ignore the charges". [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-orders-arrest-of-top-aide-to-alexei-navalny/a-56522931 (DW)]
*[[Attempts to overturn the 2020 United States presidential election]], [[Trump–Raffensperger phone call]]
**[[Fulton County, Georgia|Fulton County]] District Attorney [[Fani Willis]] opens a [[2020 Georgia election investigation|criminal investigation]] into former [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] for attempting to overturn [[Joe Biden]]'s victory in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]], including conducting a phone call with [[Georgia Secretary of State|Secretary of State]] [[Brad Raffensperger]] where he pressured Raffensperger to "find enough votes" for him. [https://www.npr.org/2021/02/10/966332808/georgia-district-attorney-is-investigating-trumps-call-to-overturn-election (NPR)]
*[[Crime in the United Kingdom]]
**British [[sex offender]] [[David Wilson (sex offender)|David Wilson]] is [[sentence (law)|sentenced]] to 25 years imprisonment for 96 offences against 51 boys aged 4 to 14. [https://bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-norfolk-56009383 (BBC News)]
*The [[Saudi government]] releases [[Women's rights in Saudi Arabia|women's rights]] activist [[Loujain al-Hathloul]] from prison, after being held in custody for almost three years. She will still be banned from traveling for the next five years, and has been placed on a three-year [[probation]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/10/saudi-activist-loujain-al-hathloul-released-from-prison (Al Jazeera)] 

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Twitter suspensions]]
**[[Social media use by Donald Trump|Donald Trump on social media]], [[2024 United States presidential election]]
***[[Twitter]] confirms that the ban on Donald Trump's account will remain permanent, even if he were to run for president in 2024. [https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/twitter-uphold-permanent-ban-against-trump-even-if-he-were-n1257269 (NBC News)]
*[[Chinese space program]]
**The [[China National Space Administration]] [[space probe]] [[Tianwen-1]] enters into [[planetary orbit]] around [[Mars]]. It is the first Chinese spacecraft to reach Mars. A [[Mars rover|rover]] will be deployed to explore the [[Martian surface]] sometime in May. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-56013041 (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020–21 in English football]]
**Following their 3–1 win against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] in the [[2020–21 FA Cup#Fifth Round Proper|fifth round]] of the [[2020–21 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] sets a [[Football records and statistics in England|record]] for the most consecutive wins in all competitions by a [[2020–21 Premier League|top-flight]] [[List of football clubs in England|English football club]], with 15 consecutive wins. [https://www.rappler.com/sports/football/manchester-city-racks-up-record-15th-straight-win (Rappler)]
